messages.subject: RE: threshold test
parts:
Dear Matthieu and tsdyn users,

I use the following commands to 268 log price pairs.

P <- cbind(P1,P2)

vec_1 <- VECM(P, lag=lags, r=1, include="none", estim="2OLS", LRinclude="const")

vec_2 <- VECM(P, lag=lags, r=1, include="none", estim="ML", LRinclude="const")

vec_3 <- VECM(P, lag=lags, r=1, include="const", estim="2OLS", LRinclude="none")

vec_4 <- VECM(P, lag=lags, r=1, include="const", estim="ML", LRinclude="none")

 

Hansen1 <- TVECM.HStest(P, lag=lags, fixed.beta=-vec_1$model.specific$coint[2], nboot=300)

Hansen2 <- TVECM.HStest(P, lag=lags, fixed.beta=-vec_2$model.specific$coint[2], nboot=300)

Hansen3 <- TVECM.HStest(P, lag=lags, fixed.beta=-vec_3$model.specific$coint[2], nboot=300)

Hansen4 <- TVECM.HStest(P, lag=lags, fixed.beta=-vec_4$model.specific$coint[2], nboot=300)

 

Seo1 <- TVECM.SeoTest(P, lag=lags, beta=-vec_1$model.specific$coint[2], nboot=200, plot=FALSE,check=FALSE)

Seo2 <- TVECM.SeoTest(P, lag=lags, beta=-vec_2$model.specific$coint[2], nboot=200, plot=FALSE,check=FALSE)

Seo3 <- TVECM.SeoTest(P, lag=lags, beta=-vec_4$model.specific$coint[2], nboot=200, plot=FALSE,check=FALSE)

I observe 2 things.

1.       I reject null hypothesis more using 2OLS than using ML estimation procedure. I know they won’t be exact, but I’m expecting that they should not be this different.

To be exact, out of 268 runs, I get

                                    p-val<=0.1                         p-val<=0.05

Hansen 1 = 21% rejection                  10%

Hansen 2 = 12% rejection                  6%

Hansen 3 = 18% rejection                  10%

Hansen 4 = 12% rejection                  5%

 

2.       OLS and ML estimates in Seo test differ as well. Seo test also rejects more than Hansen test.

                                p-val<=0.1                             p-val<=0.05

Seo 1 = 8% rejection                           6%

Seo 2 = 34% rejection                         26%

Seo 3 = 33% rejection                         27%

 

I’m not sure how to reconcile these results. Do I just increase nboot for Seo? At 200, it already took me 5 days.

I’m okay with Hansen test, but I just want to be sure I’m doing it right. My research is on threshold price transmission, so I have to make sure this test works, before I proceed to my next step.

Any thoughts? Has anyone made same observations?

Best, Nelissa

PS. I’m an R beginner.

messages.author: 8c45483022d450d5
messages.subject: Re: threshold test
parts:
Hi Nelissa

Thank you for sharing your results with us!

So for the reasons regarding why you have differences between OLS and MLE, I must say I have no clue... Maybe look at the average differences between OLS and MLE? Is is that one is systematically lower/higher than the other in your sample? Note that one usually will prefer the MLE, given the fact that the OLS is biased in small sample. You could also try a third estimator, the lead and lags OLS of Saikonnen, which does, by adding leads and lags in the first step, reduce the bias.

Now for the differences between the two tests, note that they do not have the same null! HS null is coint, while Seo null is no coint! So in that sense it is not surprising that the results are different... but do you have strong disagreements between these tests? Rather than the overall rejections, what is the percentage of cases with disagreement?

Best

Mat

messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] Re: threshold test
parts:
Hi Nelissa:
 
have you taken a look to the threshold results obtained on your OLS and MLE estimations? If I understand your code correctly, you used the threshold estimated value and use it on both tests,  right?  hence if the threshold estimations from your OLS and MLE are quite different the test results will be as well. As for the test results, besides that you are testing two different hypotheses, also take into account that the tests consider different number of regimes, the HS test considers a two regime TVECM, while the Seo considers a three regimes TVECM, there is a Master thesis from someone in Norway who developed an extention of the HS test to a three regime model, do not remember the author, but will get back to you once I recall it, you can use such a modification of the HS test if you think that your data belong to a three regime TVECM, as for the Seo test I am not aware of any extention to a two regime TVECM. 
 
Say hi to all the guys in Goettingen, hope to see you sometime during March,
 
best,
 
Sergio Rene
